messages:
eli.support: FYI escalated case #7891 — customer reports 401 only after bundling our Node SDK into their browser bundle. Works in local node dev, fails after build. Logs show Authorization header missing on outbound requests. Any quick ideas? :warning:

customer-cto: Stack: Next.js (webpack), node 18, building client for browser, using @redwood/sdk v2.1.0. Repro steps:
1) npx create-next-app
2) npm i @redwood/sdk
3) import { Client } from '@redwood/sdk'
4) const c = new Client({ apiKey: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_REDWOOD_KEY })
5) await c.generate({ prompt }) -> 401 from api.redwood-inference.com

It works if I run the same code in node (ts-node). Only fails after webpack bundle.

sam.engineer: Can you paste the import line, package.json exports block, and any webpack/esbuild config? Also copy the request headers from the failing build (network tab or server logs).

customer-cto: Paste of relevant bits:
```json
{
  "name": "customer-app",
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood/sdk": "2.1.0"
  },
  "scripts": {"build": "next build"}
}
```
Import line: `import { Client } from '@redwood/sdk'`
Webpack: standard next/webpack, no special aliasing. Network tab shows request to https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate with headers: `Content-Type: application/json` but no `Authorization` header. In server logs the SDK prints `authorization: undefined` just before the fetch.

maria.eng: Quick theory — bundler is resolving to the ESM entry and our conditional exports mean the runtime path used by the bundle is `dist/esm/index.mjs` which exports a named `Client` but the bundler's transform (or tree-shaking) is altering how the class is referenced, causing the constructor wrapper that attaches the API key to never run. I've seen similar behavior when a package has both `exports` conditional fields and a separate CJS build. Workarounds to confirm: 1) import directly from CJS: `import Client from '@redwood/sdk/dist/cjs'` (or `const Client = require('@redwood/sdk')` in a Node-only build) — does the header appear then? 2) Add a webpack alias to force `@redwood/sdk` -> `@redwood/sdk/dist/cjs/index.cjs`

Also please try building with `NODE_ENV=production next build` locally and inspect the bundle (or run `npx source-map-explorer`) to see which file is actually packaged.

maria.eng: Minimal repro we use for packaging triage (fs):
```
// index.mjs (bundled)
import { Client } from '@redwood/sdk'
const c = new Client({ apiKey: 'testkey' })
console.log('auth', c._opts?.apiKey)
```
In a repro we saw `auth undefined` only when the bundler picked the `esm` entry.

packaging-bot: Created PKG-432: "conditional exports + bundler -> missing auth header in browser bundles". Assigned to packaging team. Requested: minimal repo, exact next/webpack version, and a small repro bundle or source-map.

eli.support: Customer tried the CJS direct import workaround and reported back: partial success — headers present and requests succeed. They said switching to `import Client from '@redwood/sdk/dist/cjs'` fixed the 401 locally. Can we make an official patch (short-term) to the package exports to ensure browser bundlers pick a compatible entry (or add a UMD/browser field) so customers don't have to special-case?

maria.eng: Agreed. Short-term action: add "browser" condition in exports to point to an ESM bundle that preserves constructor side-effects, and add a note in changelog about bundler workarounds. Long-term: publish a small UMD/browser build and update tests to run a webpack bundle test per release. I'll attach a PR to PKG-432.

customer-cto: Thanks — workaround works for now. Happy to test a patch/alpha.

eli.support: Closing loop — assigning follow-up to packaging team and will update the customer when PKG-432 has an alpha. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
